content:
marie: Flagging a UX regression noticed in the compact dashboards: x-axis labels on 2-up small-multiples drop to an ellipsis and the unit disappears. This trips up readouts (e.g., 1200 -> could be ms, reqs, or bytes). dylan: Saw it too. On narrow view the label becomes `1.2k…` with no unit. Hover shows full text but that doesn't help keyboard users or screen readers. priya: Quick accessibility note: NVDA reads the visible text, so truncation equals loss of unit. We need the semantic unit preserved in the DOM even if visually shortened. taylor: Options brainstorm: a) allow two-line axis labels (reduces density), b) keep short visual label + stable micro-unit below the axis, c) show unit in legend only. I'm leaning toward (b). marie: (b) seems best for glanceability across many charts. Micro-unit must be small and consistent across charts so rows align. Also add aria-hidden on the visual micro text and full unit in aria-label on the axis container. aria-bot: A11y checklist: 1) axis group tabindex=0 for focus, 2) aria-label contains "label, unit" full text, 3) visual micro-unit elements aria-hidden, 4) tooltip reachable via keyboard. priya: Also ensure we don't repeat the unit twice to screen readers. If legend already reads it, avoid duplication. Use aria-describedby to point to a single hidden element with the full readout. dylan: On smoothing: some dashboards auto-enable smoothing at small widths which alters peak shapes. Users reported missing latency spikes. We should not change raw data by default. If smoothing is applied, mark it visibly. marie: Agreed. Add a micro-badge near top-left of chart that reads "Smoothed" when active and a keyboard-accessible toggle in the chart settings. When toggled announce change via aria-live. priya: Implementation snippet proposal for live announcement: ```html
Smoothing enabled
``` marie: For outliers: proposal to avoid automatic inset charts. Instead add a clipped-sentinel marker at the axis edge and a tooltip that shows the original outlier value + a tiny sparkline. That keeps layout simple. dylan: Tooltip content should be accessible: include the true value, timestamp, and note that the chart is clipped. For visuals, tiny sparkline can be inline SVG in the tooltip. priya: QA checklist: test keyboard focus order, ensure micro-units don't break focusable elements, validate voiceover and NVDA read full label+unit, test at 3 breakpoints (>=1280, 768-1279, <=767). taylor: Dev concerns: adding DOM for every axis can have perf implications on very large dashboards. Suggest we implement micro-unit as a single shared layer that mirrors unit labels for visible charts (virtualized). If not possible, keep DOM minimal (span with aria-hidden). marie: Decision (tentative): implement micro-unit under axis (visual-only, aria-hidden) + axis container gets aria-label with full text; add Smoothed badge and keyboard toggle; outlier sentinel + accessible tooltip with sparkline. Priya to own a11y copy, Dylan to do prototype, Taylor to evaluate perf. priya: I'll write the aria-label patterns and hidden-description component. Example aria-label: "Average latency: 1.2k milliseconds" and hidden description id for screen readers with expanded unit text. dylan: I'll open a prototype PR with CSS for micro-labels and the smoothed badge. Initial CSS: ```css .axis-micro { font-size: 11px; color: var(--muted); max-width: 56px; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .chart-badge { font-size: 10px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.06); padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 2px; } ``` marie: Thanks — please drop mocks in #design-review and tag @dylan when PR is up. If any objections to the micro-unit + sentinel approach call out now. :thumbsup: priYa: +1 from a11y (with QA steps listed). dylan: +1 from eng, will prototype. taylor: +1 from perf after initial check. marie: Closing this thread, will follow up with Figma and acceptance criteria later today.
